subject: Proposal: Dedicated go-live window & sanity lab schedule
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@novahealth.com>; Ops Team <ops@novahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:04:00 -0000
Subject: Proposal: Dedicated go-live window & sanity lab schedule

Hi Claire / NovaHealth ops,

Thanks again for the detailed call today. Per our discussion I sketched a pragmatic validation + go-live cadence that balances your traffic ramp with Redwood's dedicated provisioning timelines. High level: a two-week validation corridor (sanity labs + throughput stress), then a 72-hour canary window, followed by a production cutover slot.

Attached: sanity_lab_matrix.xlsx (test matrix by route/sequence length) and sizing-runbook-v1.pdf (how we validate steady-state throughput). Key asks from your side:
- Confirm the peak QPS and 95th-percentile latency SLO you want validated (we used 120 qps and 250ms p95 in the workbook).
- Provide 48 hours of representative traffic replay or a synthetic load profile prior to lab start.
- Point person on your side for immediate go/no-go decisioning during canary.

Proposed timeline (US region):
1) Validation corridor week A: smoke + prefix cache verification (day 1-3), steady-state throughput tests (day 4-7)
2) Validation corridor week B: model edge cases, long-sequence stress, failover drills (day 8-14)
3) Canary window (72h) where a small % of traffic is routed to Dedicated capacity with throttles in place
4) Production cutover: planned 3–4 hour blackout window with rollback plan if SLAs degrade

I've also added a HubSpot link to this thread for the DH-3621 deal. If that timeline looks reasonable I can lock resources and coordinate Redwood infra for the exact calendar days.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Strategic Account Exec | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: sanity_lab_matrix.xlsx, sizing-runbook-v1.pdf
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@novahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@novahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Dedicated go-live window & sanity lab schedule

Karthik,

Appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 120 qps peak number is roughly what we expect for steady ramp but our heaviest flows (clinical-doc summarization) can hit 180 qps bursts for a few minutes. Can your stress profile include 200 qps short spikes?
- Latency target: we care about token-level latency for the summarization route; p95 <= 300ms is acceptable but please show p50/p95 tail behavior across sequence lengths.
- We can provide 72 hours of replay data; ops will also stand up a synthetic harness if you want to inject edge cases.

Our point person for go/no-go will be Ben Thomas (CC'd on my internal list; I'll introduce him formally once we lock dates). For now please assume Ben and our platform lead will be on-call during the canary.

One ask: can Redwood run an initial lightweight validation (one business day) before your heavier week-long corridor? That lets us catch obvious config mismatches early.

Thanks,
Claire
Director of Platform Engineering | NovaHealth

Claire / team — thanks for the notes. Quick operational mapping below and a suggested tightened schedule that includes the one-day lightweight run you requested.

Operational checklist (owner in parentheses):
- Preflight: config parity check (Monica) — verify model variants, quantization profiles, and routing policies.
- Data: replay ingestion + anonymization gating (NovaHealth ops) — provide replay blob and sample schema.
- Sanity Lab Day 0 (lightweight, 1 business day): basic routing + token-level latency check at 50% expected load (Monica + Aditya).
- Sanity Lab Week (7 days): progressive ramp to 120 qps steady, 200 qps spike tests at controlled intervals (Aditya leads stress tests).
- Failover drills: region failover simulation + KV cache cold-start (Neha leads).
- Canary config: 5% traffic for 72h, progressively increase to 20% if stable (Karthik to coordinate).
- Cutover MOP (runbook): final snapshot, DNS TTL plan, monitoring runbooks, rollback criteria (Monica).

Proposed calendar (target week starting Oct 26, US):
- Oct 26: Sanity Lab Day 0 (lightweight)
- Oct 27–Nov 2: Sanity Lab Week (progressive ramp, stress windows on Oct 29 & Nov 1)
- Nov 3–5: Canary window (72h)
- Nov 6: Production cutover slot (3–4 hour blackout window)

I've attached a concise MOP template and will draft the cutover checklist as we lock dates. If NovaHealth wants earlier dates we can try to accelerate, but we need two business days for infra prep to reserve the dedicated pool.

Monica
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachment reference: final-mop.docx (draft will follow)

Claire / Ben — thanks for aligning. Per Claire's preference and our infra availability, we've locked the calendar below. Please confirm Ben is the escalation lead for canary decisions.

Finalized timeline (US region):
- Oct 26: Sanity Lab Day 0 (lightweight pass, 50% load)
- Oct 27–Nov 2: Full validation corridor (progressive ramp, scheduled stress windows Oct 29 & Nov 1)
- Nov 3 00:00 UTC–Nov 5 23:59 UTC: Canary window (5% -> 20% traffic as stability gates pass)
- Nov 6 02:00–06:00 UTC: Production cutover slot (3–4 hour maintenance window).

Cutover guardrails (short):
- Clear rollback criteria: sustained p95 latency > 350ms for 15 minutes OR error rate > 1.5% for 10 minutes triggers immediate rollback.
- Monitoring: token-level latency dashboards, per-route error heatmaps, and per-host GPU utilization.
- Communication channels: Slack channel #dh-3621-cutover (Redwood + NovaHealth), phone bridge + Doc link for runbook.

Next steps for Monday: Monica will post the MOP and a final checklist. Ben / Claire — please confirm your on-call roster for Nov 3–6 and reply to this thread. Once we have that I will mark DH-3621 as committed in HubSpot and reserve the dedicated pool.

Cheers,
